I am a PhD candidate in Education Policy at the University of Virginia and an Institute of Education Sciences (IES) pre-doctoral fellow. My dissertation focuses on new technologies in schools, asking two questions: **do they actually help students**, and **can we trust the data we use to decide?**

## Working Papers

- [Generalizing Beyond the Regression Discontinuity Cutoff Using Panel Data: An Evaluation of Hybrid Tutoring](chapters/ch1/index.qmd)
- [Reliable Measurement of Teachers' Instructional Practices with LLM Classifiers](chapters/ch2/index.qmd)

## Published Work

- Cohen, J., Jones, N., Wong, V. C., Quinn, A., Erickson, S., Parten, H., & Suhr, M. (in press). Practice-based, online modules for expediting teacher skill development. *Educational Evaluation and Policy Analysis*. [EdWorkingPaper No. 26-1460](https://doi.org/10.26300/vp80-mq53)
- Cohen, J., Wong, V. C., Krishnamachari, A., & Erickson, S. (2024). Experimental evidence on the robustness of coaching supports in teacher education. *Educational Researcher, 53*(1), 19–35.
- Suhr, M., Erickson, S., Kelcey, B., Mclean, L., Cohen, J., & Jones, N. (2026). Exploring the use of performance tasks as formative assessments of pre-service teacher instructional skills within teacher preparation programs. *Educational Assessment*.
- Wilson, K., Cohen, J., & Erickson, S. (2025). Teacher candidates' perceptions of mixed reality simulations: Variations by task, support, and mode of delivery. *AERA Open, 11*, 23328584251375064.
